dedupe_keys.name: valuing bicycling s economic and health impacts in wisconsin university of wisconsin madison 2010

description: This January 2010 report, prepared for Wisconsin Representative Spencer Black by Maggie Grabow, Micah Hahn and Melissa Whited at the University of Wisconsin-Madison's Nelson Institute, estimates the value of bicycling to Wisconsin's economy and health. Contents: bicycle person-days (about 13 million) and average spending by resident and non-resident cyclists by activity type, fed into the IMPLAN input-output model; the total economic impact of bicycle recreation and tourism is about $924 million with 13,193 full-time-equivalent jobs, split into direct, indirect and induced effects for residents and visitors; a second part values health benefits of replacing short car trips with bicycle trips (fitness, air quality) at about $410 million, plus greenhouse gas mitigation; a third reviews bicycling demographics. Coverage: Wisconsin. Format and access: a free 42-page PDF with tables and appendices. Licence and cost: free; no licence stated. Caveats: 2010 estimates from survey-based assumptions; the authors list limitations. The spending and job multipliers can value lost cycling activity when trails or bike routes are disrupted, for economic loss in capacity planning and resilience studies. It relates to Strava Metro in the catalogue.
